title: The Fox Wedding
text: Rain falls from a clear sky, warm as tears. Through the wood comes a procession of foxes in silk walking upright, carrying lanterns and a bride in a red veil. It is very bad luck, the old wives say, to be seen watching.

options.label: Look away and hide, and pray the foxes never knew you were there.

outcomes.text: The procession passes and the rain stops. Where they walked lies a dropped wedding gift, a heavy silk purse.
The procession passes and the rain stops. One fox turns back to look straight at your hiding place, smiling; it will remember you.

options.label: Leave a gift for the fox bride, as the old wives say you should.

outcomes.text: A fox returns alone in silk, bearing a gift of its own, and bows. Luck follows you out of the wood.

options.label: The stealthiest watches the procession, curious where the foxes walk.

outcomes.text: Unseen, they learn the foxes' secret road.
They are seen. The bride lifts her veil and smiles; beneath it is nothing but teeth.
